# PDF verification

> Verifies an uploaded file is a structurally sound PDF and reports the first failing check by a stable identifier

- **System:** [pdf-service](../index.md#pdf-service)
- **Caller:** External — the caller is outside the trust boundary
- **Blast radius:** Medium
- **Source:** [`pdf-verify.yamlet.yaml`](../../../trace-fixtures/pdf-verify.yamlet.yaml)

Reads the bytes of an untrusted upload and applies seven structural checks in a fixed precedence order. It returns the validated PDF or the identifier of the earliest failing check; it stores nothing.

## Contract

`pdf-verify` — check an upload is a well-formed PDF and return it or the earliest failing check

- **Inputs:** `file`, `filename`
- **Outputs:** `pdf_file`, `error`

## Requirements

<a id="rq-1"></a>

### RQ-1 · The service accepts a well-formed upload and returns it

<a id="ac-1"></a>
**AC-1** · When `file` named `filename` passes every structural check, the system shall:

- return `pdf_file` to the caller
- preserve `filename` as the name of the returned PDF

<a id="rq-2"></a>

### RQ-2 · The service rejects an unsafe filename

<a id="ac-2"></a>
**AC-2** · If `filename` contains a path separator, a parent-directory traversal component or a control character, then the system shall:

- set `error` to unsafe_filename
- return no `pdf_file`

<a id="ac-3"></a>
**AC-3** · If `filename` is empty, then the system shall:

- set `error` to unsafe_filename
- return no `pdf_file`

<a id="rq-3"></a>

### RQ-3 · The service bounds the upload size

<a id="ac-4"></a>
**AC-4** · If `file` is larger than `<max_size_bytes>` bytes, then the system shall:

- set `error` to too_large
- return no `pdf_file`

Examples:

| `<max_size_bytes>` |
|---|
| 10485760 |

<a id="ac-5"></a>
**AC-5** · When `file` is exactly `<max_size_bytes>` bytes, the system shall:

- set `error` to an empty value

Examples:

| `<max_size_bytes>` |
|---|
| 10485760 |

<a id="rq-4"></a>

### RQ-4 · The service checks the header and trailer markers

<a id="ac-6"></a>
**AC-6** · If `file` does not begin with the bytes %PDF-1., then the system shall:

- set `error` to invalid_header

<a id="ac-7"></a>
**AC-7** · If the last 1024 bytes of `file` contain no %%EOF marker, then the system shall:

- set `error` to missing_eof

<a id="rq-5"></a>

### RQ-5 · The service checks the cross-reference table and object structure

Decided by [ADR-0001 · Structural PDF parsing](../decisions/ADR-0001-structural-pdf-parsing.md) (accepted)

<a id="ac-8"></a>
**AC-8** · If no startxref offset in `file` resolves to a cross-reference table or stream followed by a trailer dictionary containing /Root, then the system shall:

- set `error` to invalid_xref_trailer

Decided by [ADR-0002 · Isolation of structural parsing](../decisions/ADR-0002-isolation-of-structural-parsing.md) (proposed)

<a id="ac-9"></a>
**AC-9** · If `file` contains unbalanced obj and endobj delimiters or an unclosed dictionary or stream token, then the system shall:

- set `error` to invalid_object_structure

<a id="rq-6"></a>

### RQ-6 · The service reports only the earliest failing check

<a id="ac-10"></a>
**AC-10** · If 2 or more structural checks fail for `file`, then the system shall:

- evaluate all seven checks independently of each other
- set `error` to the identifier of the earliest failing check in the order unsafe_filename, too_large, invalid_header, missing_eof, invalid_xref_trailer, invalid_object_structure
- return no `pdf_file`
